latency la·ten·cy | ˈlātnsē | noun 1 the state of existing but not yet being developed or manifest; concealment: tension, and the latency of violence, make the greatest impressions. • the state of a disease not yet manifesting the usual symptoms: the latency of tumors in mice | [as modifier] : the disease's latency period can last up to five years. 2 Computing the delay before a transfer of data begins following an instruction for its transfer: poor performance due to network latency | [as modifier] : subscribers can expect some latency time when issuing a request | there are several ways to minimize rotational latencies.
